staffing_plan.notes: PM is critical path owner for T6 (stakeholder validation), T24 (UAT prep), T29 (documentation), T30 (go-live), T32 (sign-off). Must be 80% dedicated during Phase 2-3 sprints per R5 mitigation. Allocation 11.6% is within 10-15% PM oversight rule (500 total hours × 10-15% = 50-75h; 58h is within range).

Backend Developer owns critical path tasks T1, T3, T5, T8, T11, T14, T17, T20, T23 (9 tasks, 57 days zero slack). Must be 80% dedicated Phase 2-3 per R5 mitigation. Allocation 56% reflects actual hours; however, critical path concentration requires full-time focus during Phases 2-3 (weeks 2-7). Flag: If allocation appears low, it is because total project hours (500h) include QA and PM overhead; Backend Developer's actual sprint capacity is higher. Recommend scheduling Backend Developer at 80% minimum during critical path execution.

Frontend Developer owns critical path task T8 (real-time KPI widget UI) and contributes to T4, T9, T12, T14. Allocation 22% is conservative; actual sprint utilization will be 60-70% during Phase 2 per project plan. Risk R9 flags potential overallocation if UI tasks accumulate > 2 sprints backlog. Mitigation: Prioritize UC2, UC3, UC5, UC6 UI first; use component library. Contingency: If overallocated, hire contract UI developer or defer UC4 export polish to Phase 3.

QA Engineer owns critical path tasks T17 (end-to-end integration test), T20 (regression test), and contributes to T2, T22, T25, T27. Total QA hours (124h) = 24.8% of total project hours (500h). Development effort (Backend 280h + Frontend 110h = 390h). QA minimum per PMBOK 8.2 = 390h × 25% = 97.5h. Actual QA allocation 124h > 97.5h minimum: PASSES QA staffing rule. No QA under-allocation risk.

open_questions.question: Is the Email Service (A3) an existing internal or third-party SMTP service with documented API and SLA, or does it require custom build? (Assumption A1 validation)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If email service does not exist or requires custom build, Phase 2 scope expands by 1-2 weeks (40-80 hours); if SLA is undefined, 90% on-time delivery metric becomes unachievable. Risk R1 (HIGH) depends on this answer.

open_questions.question: What is the scope of PagerDuty integration: webhook-based alert delivery only, or does it include custom escalation policy, on-call scheduling, or incident lifecycle management? (Assumption A2 validation)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If PagerDuty integration scope is broader than webhook ingestion, Phase 2 scope expands by 1-2 weeks (30-60 hours); alert response time metric (< 1 hour) may require PagerDuty SLA validation. Risk R2 (HIGH) depends on this answer.

open_questions.question: Can the current PostgreSQL database support 15-minute refresh cadence with polling or scheduled queries, or does the team need to architect a data warehouse or streaming pipeline? (Assumption A3 validation)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If database performance is poor or data volume is high, team must pivot to data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) or streaming architecture, adding 3-4 weeks to Phase 2 and increasing budget by $10K-$20K. Risk R3 (HIGH) depends on this answer.

open_questions.question: Is a dedicated Product Owner (80% allocation minimum) formally assigned and available for sprint planning, backlog refinement, and scope trade-offs during Phase 2-3 sprints?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires clear PO ownership for sprint planning and backlog refinement; without this, sprint cycles will stall on scope decisions. Risk R4 (HIGH) and R5 (HIGH) depend on this answer.

open_questions.question: Is the Backend Developer (280 hours, critical path owner) formally committed to 80% allocation through 2025-04-10, with written sign-off from resource manager?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If Backend Developer is pulled off critical path due to competing priorities, critical path tasks will slip and project deadline will be missed. Risk R5 (HIGH) depends on this answer.

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 68.0 because the project has well-defined requirements (HIGH input quality), clear success metrics, and a realistic 12-week timeline with 15% buffer. However, five HIGH-scored risks (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R11) create significant execution uncertainty: Email Service and PagerDuty integration scope are unvalidated, PostgreSQL performance is unproven for 15-minute refresh, Product Owner availability is not confirmed, and Backend Developer critical path allocation is not secured. Three unvalidated assumptions (A1, A2, A3) further reduce confidence. Hybrid SDLC requires active stakeholder engagement and sprint discipline, which depends on PO availability (R4). Mitigation: Resolve open questions 1-5 in Week 1 discovery before Sprint 1 kickoff; secure written resource commitments for Backend Developer and PM; validate Email Service, PagerDuty, and PostgreSQL in sandbox environment.

project_viability.analysis: Project deadline is 2025-04-10 (12 weeks from 2025-01-10). Critical path duration is 57 days (8.1 weeks) with 15% buffer applied = 9.3 weeks total. Deadline allows 12 weeks; critical path + buffer = 9.3 weeks. Slack = 12 - 9.3 = 2.7 weeks (19 days). Project is within deadline but AT_RISK because: (1) Five HIGH-scored risks (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R11) can each cause 1-2 week slips; (2) Critical path has zero slack on 9 tasks (T1, T3, T5, T8, T11, T14, T17, T20, T23); (3) Any critical path task slip > 3 days triggers R11 mitigation (descope Phase 2 features). If any two HIGH risks materialize (e.g., Email Service requires custom build + PostgreSQL performance pivot), critical path will exceed deadline. Contingency per R11: Descope UC5 (scheduled delivery) and UC6 (alerting) to Phase 3; deliver UC2 (real-time KPI), UC3 (custom report), UC4 (export) by 2025-04-10.

scoping_options.title: Descope Phase 2 integrations (UC5, UC6) to Phase 3
scoping_options.description: Deliver Phase 1 (discovery) + UC2 (real-time KPI), UC3 (custom report), UC4 (export) by 2025-04-10. Defer UC5 (scheduled delivery) and UC6 (alerting) to Phase 3 post-launch. Reduces Phase 2 scope by ~50 hours (T12, T13, T14, T15). Removes Email Service (R1) and PagerDuty (R2) integration risk from critical path. Allows 4-week Phase 2 instead of 4.5 weeks.
scoping_options.risk_mitigation: Eliminates R1 and R2 from critical path; reduces critical path duration to 7.6 weeks + 15% buffer = 8.7 weeks. Provides 3.3-week schedule buffer. Trade-off: CSMs lose scheduled delivery and alerting at launch; adoption may be lower initially.

scoping_options.title: Add contract Backend Developer (50% allocation) for Phase 2-3
scoping_options.description: Hire contract Backend Developer at 50% allocation (140 hours) to share critical path load with primary Backend Developer. Reduces primary Backend Developer allocation from 56% to 42% and provides capacity buffer for risk mitigation. Estimated cost: $35K-$50K (140 hours × $250-$350/hour contractor rate). Allows parallel execution of T7, T10, T13, T15 (Email Service, PagerDuty, report generation, alert engine).
scoping_options.risk_mitigation: Reduces critical path duration by 0.5 weeks through parallelization. Mitigates R5 (Backend Developer overallocation) and provides contingency capacity if primary developer is pulled off project. Trade-off: Increases budget by $35K-$50K; requires onboarding time (3-5 days).

scoping_options.title: Extend deadline to 2025-05-10 (16 weeks)
scoping_options.description: Request 4-week deadline extension to 2025-05-10. Provides 16-week total timeline vs. 12 weeks. Critical path (9.3 weeks) + buffer = 10.7 weeks; slack = 5.3 weeks (37 days). Eliminates schedule risk entirely. Allows sequential execution of Phase 2 features without parallelization pressure.
scoping_options.risk_mitigation: Eliminates R11 (critical path schedule slip) and provides 5.3-week schedule buffer for risk mitigation. Allows Email Service and PagerDuty integration to be validated and implemented without time pressure. Trade-off: Delays CSM adoption by 4 weeks; may impact business case if CSMs are losing 10 hours/week to manual reporting.
